newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen up on more foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen up on more foreign buying.

text.p: Thai stocks, which rallied sharply on Friday, are seen rising further on Monday on more anticipated foreign buying, brokers said.

"More capital inflows from foreign countries are seen coming into Thailand after the government last week changed its baht system to a managed float system. The buying mood by foreigners is seen outweighting selling," said Padermpob Songkroh of Nava Finance and Securities.
The composite SET index closed 39.11 points higher to 657.09 on 16.8 billion baht turnover on Friday. The SET-50 index rose 3.43 points to 49.16.
Total net buying by foreigners on Friday amounted to 4.8 billion baht.

Foreigners had been buying stocks actively since last Wednesday, the day the Thai government changed the currency to the managed float which led foreigners to believe stocks prices had become cheaper by at least 10 percent.
